# `Scanner/ProtocolToSpec-v0` · Adapt the standard protocol until the examination meets its specification

**Status:** PRACTICE: level(s) 1, 3 admitted; fixed_recipe#2 passes 25 of 300 (upper bound 11.4 % > 10 %)

The everyday protocol question: the standard protocol misses the specification on this patient, what has to change? One scan of the standard protocol shows which requirement fails; the budget then pays for one more scan, and which one is worth making (another inversion time or another echo time) depends on the first. By level: level 1 is a measurement task, level 2 is a measurement task, level 3 is a measurement task (a fixed list of scans with a fixed solver passes this many points below the reference: -1.7 at level 1, 0 at level 2, 20.7 at level 3; 300 instances per level; 25 points or more make a decision task).

Kind of task: **{'kind': 'measurement', 'levels': {'1': 'measurement', '2': 'measurement', '3': 'measurement'}, 'evidence': 'reference minus open_loop, points of pass rate: -1.7 at level 1, 0 at level 2, 20.7 at level 3 (n = 300 per level, engine mrgym-engine-0.2.0)'}**.

```python
import mrgym
env = mrgym.make("Scanner/ProtocolToSpec-v0", level=3, seed=0)
obs, info = env.reset()
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A test object with vials of hidden materials; the scanner; the standard protocol of a two-image inversion-recovery examination; a scan-time budget for the standard protocol at low resolution and one repeat of it | For each of the two images: inversion time, echo time and number of averages (the averages share one scan-time limit) | Noise-free scans of the delivered protocols on the hidden object with the analytic noise of the hidden receiver: a T1 contrast ratio, a T2 contrast ratio and an SNR must hold for each image, and the scan times of the two images together must stay within a limit |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (a disc of gel with vials), 1.5 T
- Sequences that matter here: ir, se
- Formulas the agent is given: from the datasheet: the inversion-recovery spin-echo signal mechanism (signed recovery with the inversion time, exp(-TE / T2), the slice profile), the scan-time rule, noise variance proportional to the receiver bandwidth. Not given: how SNR scales with voxel size, lines and averages, and the statistics of the magnitude of noise

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| T1, T2 and proton density of every material | the geometry and the standard protocol of the images |
| receiver noise level | the four requirements of each image and their regions |
| transmit gain and B1 pattern | which region of the T1 pair is to be nulled and which region of the T2 pair has the longer T2 |
| receive profile | the definition of SNR |
| off-resonance field | the instrument datasheet |
| which requirement the standard protocol misses | realised protocol, timing and cost of every plan and scan |
| the 128-bit world seed |  |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'A': {'ti_ms': '<milliseconds>', 'te_ms': '<milliseconds>', 'averages': '<integer>'}, 'B': {'ti_ms': '<milliseconds>', 'te_ms': '<milliseconds>', 'averages': '<integer>'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts both delivered scans
- Error: `minus the margin of the examination: the smallest of ln(achieved / required) over the requirements of both images (for the scan time ln(allowed / planned)); negative exactly when every requirement holds`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates and, for each image, T1 contrast >= 4, T2 contrast >= 1.5, SNR >= 20 ; and the scan times of the two images together <= the stated limit

## What the agent reads at reset (level 3, seed 0)

~~~text
# Adapt the standard protocol until the examination meets its specification
A test object with vials of unknown materials lies in the field of
view. The examination has 2 inversion-recovery spin-echo images, A and B, with the same geometry and repetition time:
    sequence ir, tr_ms 400, fov_mm 240, matrix 128, slice_mm 5, bandwidth_hz_per_px 200, full k-space.
Both run with the standard protocol ti_ms 80, te_ms 12, averages 1. Each image has its own specification:
    image A
      T1 contrast   R5 at least 4 times as bright as R6 (the inversion can null R6)
      T2 contrast   R1 (the longer T2) at least 1.5 times as bright as R6
      SNR           at least 20 in R6
    image B
      T1 contrast   R1 at least 4 times as bright as R5 (the inversion can null R5)
      T2 contrast   R1 (the longer T2) at least 1.5 times as bright as R3
      SNR           at least 20 in R7
and the examination has one more: the scan times of the images together are at most 244 s.
"As bright as" compares the signals of two regions in the image. SNR of a region = magnitude of the mean complex signal of the region's pixels / standard deviation of the noise in one pixel, one channel (real or imaginary part).
On this object the standard protocol does not meet the specification. For each image you choose ti_ms, te_ms and
averages; everything else stays as above.
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre; each lies inside one homogeneous material):
  R1: y -52.62, x -22.16, radius 11.5
  R2: y 55.94, x 16.75, radius 11.5
  R3: y 47.7, x -37.57, radius 11.5
  R4: y -4.76, x -60.11, radius 11.5
  R5: y 0.58, x -3.84, radius 11.5
  R6: y 12.02, x 53.92, radius 11.5
  R7: y -44.84, x 31.23, radius 11.5
Deliver the three numbers for each image with `submit`. The images are not run in this episode: the scanner evaluates
the protocols you deliver. Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names. That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
This console adjusts itself before a scan (centre frequency, transmit gain, shim): 30 s. A scan with the same sequence
and the same field of view, slice and orientation as the scan before it reuses those adjustments and starts after
3 s; changing only timing, matrix or averages does not repeat them. `plan` shows the cost of the next scan. Nothing
about the materials, the noise or the state of the system is known in advance.

Passing: every requirement holds, evaluated on noise-free scans of your protocols with the noise level of this scanner;
the scan time of each image is what the console plans for it as a scan of its own, adjustments included. The scanner's
log must show that you measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 63 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 48 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's scans are noise-free and its noise is analytic.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
